chapter: Chapter IV: Sheaf Cohomology and Spectral Sequences

examples.title: Cech Cohomology
examples.content: For a sheaf F and open cover U = {U_i}, the Cech cohomology H^p(U, F) is computed from cochains assigning sections over p+1-fold intersections.

examples.title: Dolbeault Cohomology
examples.content: For a complex manifold, Dolbeault cohomology H^{p,q}(X) measures the failure of the dbar equation to have solutions.

simulator.title: Cohomology of the Torus
simulator.description: The torus T^2 has non-trivial H^1, reflecting its two independent cycles. Rotate to see the generators.

applications.title: Algebraic Geometry
applications.description: Sheaf cohomology computes global sections and obstructions to extending local data globally.

applications.title: Deformation Theory
applications.description: H^1 classifies infinitesimal deformations while H^2 contains obstructions.

concepts.name: Derived Functor
concepts.definition: R^iF measures the failure of a left-exact functor F to be exact, computed via injective resolutions.

concepts.name: Spectral Sequence
concepts.definition: A sequence of pages (E_r, d_r) converging to a graded object, used to compute cohomology.

exercises.question: Compute the Dolbeault cohomology H^{0,1}(CP^1) using the standard cover.
exercises.hint: Use the cover by two affine charts and the Cech-Dolbeault isomorphism.

exercises.question: Show that for a fine sheaf F on a paracompact space, H^p(X, F) = 0 for p > 0.
exercises.hint: Fine sheaves admit partitions of unity, making Cech cochains exact.

diagrams.title: Cech Nerve
diagrams.description: Visualize the simplicial complex formed by intersections of open sets.
diagrams.instructions: Each k-simplex corresponds to a non-empty (k+1)-fold intersection.
